A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RNR-DP research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including the additional appendices in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation results, baseline comparisons and component ablations in Sections 4 and 6 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds SDP comparisons, noise-schedule ablations, sampled-action analysis and SAC experiments.

M1.justification: Section 5, Algorithms 1–2 and Appendix B retain the same buffer, sequential denoising, mixture scheduling, initialization and conditioning architecture. The additional schedule variants are ablations; the proposed method is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same nine tasks from ManiSkill2, ManiSkill3 and Adroit, with unchanged observation and object-generalization coverage. The new SAC analyses vary control procedures on existing tasks. Real robots and Robosuite are discussed but not evaluated.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates Streaming Diffusion Policy only on Relocate. v2 adds SDP comparisons on PushChair with and without generalization, StackCube, TurnFaucet with and without generalization, and Hammer (Tables 16–17). This substantially broadens evaluation against the closest related method; the other baseline families remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The original benchmark protocols remain unchanged, but substantial new evaluation designs are introduced. Appendix F samples 1,000 actions from a StackCube state for PCA and density analysis. Appendix M compares ordinary SAC with four-action outputs and eight-step action repetition across three tasks.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of multimodality through sampled actions (Appendix F), alternative mixture proportions and chunk-wise scheduling (Appendix H), and task response sensitivity through SAC controls (Appendix M). These address distinct questions beyond the retained initialization, capacity and prediction-type ablations.

E5.justification: v2 introduces kernel density estimation in Appendix F and shaded bands around SAC curves in Figures 19–21. The bands' statistical meaning and the RL run counts are unspecified. The existing benchmark statement of evaluation across ten random seeds is unchanged.

E6.justification: Retained benchmark scores, including the original Relocate SDP comparison, are unchanged. v2 adds SDP results across six further task conditions, scheduling success rates of 0.001 for chunk-wise scheduling and 0.558 for the 67/33 mixture versus the retained 0.585, plus bimodality observations and SAC learning curves.

T1.justification: The diffusion equations, buffer definitions and NFEs/a formula are unchanged, with no new theorem or proof. Section 3 corrects a prose symbol from beta to gamma to match the existing equation; the added responsiveness definition is conceptual rather than formal.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same central contributions and claims of responsive and efficient control on five response-sensitive and four regular tasks. The abstract retains the 18% and 6.9% improvements; v2 merely identifies DDIM and explicitly names success rate for the latter.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the limitation about untested behavioral diversity relative to DP with the absence of real-robot evaluation, while interpreting its new action distribution as evidence of preserved multimodality. New discussions explain task grouping, buffer-horizon relationships, scheduling compatibility, prospective deployment and the exploration difficulties of long-action SAC.

D1.justification: v2 supplies project-page and comparison-video links, documents choosing buffer capacity below the minimum demonstration horizon, and describes the new sampling and SAC procedures. The architecture, hardware, training details and original hyperparameter tables remain unchanged. The links alone do not establish code availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Nakamoto et al. Cal-QL citation when discussing Adroit Pen. Appendix H also clarifies the relationship to SDP scheduling, including describing its own scheduling as a chunk-size-one special case. The main related-work discussion and overall positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: v2 substantially expands the explanatory narrative through dedicated discussions of task classification, deployment, buffer selection, scheduling, initialization and benchmark choice. It also clarifies the abstract and adds cross-references. Most existing prose and the main section order remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 16 expands, Tables 17–18 are added, and Figures 16–21 introduce density, scheduling, initialization and SAC learning-curve displays. Figure 1 gains success-rate axis labels, and existing tables and paragraphs reflow. The visual additions substantially extend the presentation.

improvement.justification: Broader SDP comparisons and new scheduling and response-sensitivity diagnostics strengthen support for the existing conclusions, while diagrams and tuning guidance improve clarity. The net gain is limited: the removed comparative-diversity caveat is only partially addressed by samples from one state without a DP comparison, and uncertainty bands in the new RL plots remain undefined.
